mathematical_defect_review.printed_claim: Hom_O(A,B) is canonically a module over Z(Gamma(X,O)) for an arbitrary sheaf of possibly noncommutative rings O.
mathematical_defect_review.reason: A globally central section need not restrict to a section commuting with every local section, because local sections need not extend globally. Left multiplication by that restriction can therefore fail to be O-linear.

counterexample_replay.space: The Sierpinski space with opens empty, U, and X.
counterexample_replay.rings: O(X)=Q[t] and O(U)=M_2(Q), with t restricting to diag(1,0).
counterexample_replay.failure: For the left regular module and the identity morphism, multiplication by diag(1,0) is not M_2(Q)-linear; with s=E_12 and m=I, D(sm)=E_12 while sD(m)=0.

mathematical_defect_review.correct_replacement: Use Gamma(X,O^natural), where O^natural is the sheaf-theoretic center consisting of sections that remain central after restriction to every smaller open subset.
mathematical_defect_review.maximality_scope: Gamma(X,O^natural) is the maximal scalar subring acting by the displayed pointwise multiplication formula on Hom_O(A,B) for every pair of left O-modules.
mathematical_defect_review.special_case: The printed formula is valid when restriction maps preserve centers, in particular when O is commutative.
